title: Normal curve points with separable residue field are smooth
statement: Let $k$ be a field and $X$ a curve over $k$ [def-pc-curve], so $X$ is integral, separated and of finite type over $k$ and has dimension one. Let $x\in X$ be a closed point with residue field $\kappa(x)$ [def-weil-residue-field]. Suppose $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is an integrally closed domain and $\kappa(x)/k$ is finite separable [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]. Then $\mathcal O_{X,x}$ is a discrete valuation ring [def-sc-discrete-valuation-ring], and the structure morphism $X\to\operatorname{Spec}k$ is smooth at $x$ [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], meaning that some open neighbourhood of $x$ is smooth over $k$. The field $k$ need not be perfect.

source.place: Tag 0B8Y, lemma-regular-point-on-curve: equivalence of normality, the DVR property and regularity at a closed point, and equivalence with smoothness when the residue field is separable over the base.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-curve-closed-point-affine-local-model] to the given curve and closed point. Choose its affine neighbourhood $U$, and put $S=\Gamma(U,\mathcal O_X)$, $R=\mathcal O_{X,x}$. It gives a maximal ideal $\mathfrak q$, a finite type $k$-algebra $S$, and a local $k$-algebra isomorphism $S_{\mathfrak q}\cong R$, with both local rings Noetherian domains of dimension one.

source.place: Tag 0B8Y, lemma-regular-point-on-curve, opening sentence of proof, expanded by Tag 0A21, lemma-dimension-locally-algebraic (2),(3); affine chart and Noetherianity details recorded in the repair report.

proof.text: The hypothesis says that $R$ is integrally closed, so it is normal. Its Noetherian local domain and dimension-one hypotheses were obtained in step 1. Apply [lem-sc-normal-dim1-dvr] to conclude that $R$ is a discrete valuation ring. Apply independently [lem-weil-pbc-regular-local-dim-one-iff-normal] to the same ring to conclude that $R$ is regular. The local-ring isomorphism of step 1 transfers regularity to $S_{\mathfrak q}$.

source.place: Tag 00PD, lemma-characterize-dvr, (5) implies (1) and (3), as used in Tag 0B8Y

proof.text: The residue-field isomorphism over $k$ in [lem-sfb-curve-closed-point-affine-local-model] identifies $\kappa(\mathfrak q)/k$ with the assumed finite separable extension $\kappa(x)/k$. Thus [lem-sfb-regular-separable-affine-smooth-neighbourhood] applies to $f$, $U$, $S$ and $\mathfrak q$, using regularity from step 2. It gives an open subscheme $V\subseteq X$ containing $x$ for which $f|_V$ is smooth. This is the required second conclusion; neither application assumes $k$ perfect.
